reason: Confirmed in-scope correctness failure. The contract (problem.txt, the operative contract here — the artifact has no test.py/get_inputs narrowing the domain, and validate_inputs itself declares all finite FP16 values legal) requires abs(actual[i] - asinh(x[i])) <= 1e-6 with zero relative tolerance over the entire legal domain. Probe t9 exhaustively swept all 30824 finite FP16 values with |x|<=1.05 (the polynomial branch), comparing kernel.run() output against FP64 torch.asinh: max absolute error 1.52e-6 > 1e-6 with 16 violations, worst at x=1.0498046875 just below the 1.05 branch boundary — exactly the location predicted by claim c1. Probe t11 independently confirmed the same 16 violations in the boundary-straddling window 0.95<=|x|<=1.15, all on the polynomial side (the log branch above 1.05 is within tolerance). This is not a rounding/accumulation-order artifact the contract excuses: the tolerance is an explicitly declared fixed absolute bound that approximations "are permitted if they satisfy ... throughout the entire legal domain," and the polynomial fails it. c2 (large-magnitude FP32 tail, up to ±65504) was rebutted with zero violations, so the defect is localized to the polynomial approximation, not the whole design. Skeptic signed off with no new claims (t15); no open or unresolved claims remain.
